records.title: Design & Analysis of JPDAF Tracker with AI-Enabled Maneuvering Models
records.funder: Prince Sultan Defense Studies and Research Center (PSDSARC)
records.description: This project, which aims to enhance radar target tracking through the integration of artificial intelligence was accepted by the Prince Sultan Defense Studies and Research Center (PSDSARC) and awarded funding of 277,150 SAR for a one-year duration. The project aims to advance target tracking capabilities by incorporating AI into the Joint Probabilistic Data Association Filter (JPDAF) algorithm. It utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)/Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to enhance performance in complex, high-acceleration scenarios while also extending functionality to bistatic and passive radar systems for increased accuracy and adaptability.

media.alt: 3D JPDAF tracking plot showing target trajectories, future tracks, missed detections, returns, and clutter.
media.caption: JPDAF tracker demonstration.

records.title: Vehicle Access Automation
records.funder: Deanship of Postgraduate Studies and Scientific Research at Qassim University
records.description: Automation is a key goal of Saudi Vision 2030; however, most vehicle gates in the country remain manual, resulting in inefficiencies and security risks. This project proposes a sustainable, computer vision–based gate automation system with strong anti-spoofing capabilities. We detect the nearest car using IoU and extract three features: (1) car make and model, (2) Saudi license plate recognition (a new contribution), and (3) face recognition. These are matched against a database, followed by a final decision via a linear SVM. The system’s strength lies in combining all three inputs, making it ideal for high-security areas like campuses and military bases. Our prototype currently achieves approximately 94% accuracy, and we aim to exceed 99% by expanding our GPU resources with additional units.

media.alt: Animated vehicle-gate scene with a detection box around an approaching vehicle.
media.caption: Vehicle-access automation demonstration.

records.title: Design and Implementation of a Novel and Robust Automated Attendance System
records.funder: Partially Funded by the Innovation and Intellectual Property Center at Qassim University
records.description: This project presents a smart and robust automated attendance system using computer vision and deep learning. Designed for educational institutions, it tracks student attendance in real-time by capturing multiple images during class, recognizing faces to mark presence, detect latecomers, and ensure students remain throughout the session. The system uses YOLOv8 for person detection and InsightFace for face recognition. Tested in real classrooms, it reduces manual effort, improves accuracy, and enhances classroom management. Compared to card-based systems and face recognition tools like FaceNet and DeepFace, it offers superior real-time tracking and continuous monitoring. With 96.30% accuracy, the system is scalable and cloud-integration-ready, making it a valuable asset for modern education.

media.alt: Classroom attendance demonstration with multiple people detected and face-recognition confidence labels.
media.caption: Automated attendance system demonstration.

records.title: Design and Implementation of a Robust Anti-Spoofing System for Vehicle Gate Access Using Recent Artificial Intelligence Techniques
records.funder: Logistically Supported by the Innovation and Intellectual Property Center at Qassim University
records.description: The system automates vehicle gate access using computer vision and machine learning. It detects the nearest vehicle via the intersection over union (IoU) and then extracts the car's make, license plate, and driver's face using three specialized models. These features are matched against an authorized database, and a linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) with a tuned threshold makes the final access decision. The system achieves 97% vehicle classification, 93.1% license plate recognition, 57% face recognition, and 97% overall classification accuracy, enabling secure, real-time, and efficient gate automation.
